newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia PM's party leads in three opinion polls.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia PM's party leads in three opinion polls.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek's Liberal Democratic Party, facing a general election on November 10, received most voter support in three opinion polls over the weekend.

But the surveys showed between 30 and 50 percent of Slovenia's 1.5 million voters were still undecided on which party to back in the country's second free election since independence from former Yugoslavia in 1991.

Support for the centre-left Liberal Democrats, the senior partner in a coalition with rightist parties for the past four years, was highest in a survey conducted by Dnevnik newspaper at 12.7 percent, slipping only one point in a separate poll in the daily Delo.
Drnovsek's party took 33 percent of votes in the last general election in 1992.

The Social Democrats, led by former defence minister Janez Jansa, emerged as the second biggest party in the three surveys with eight percent in Delo's poll to six percent in a poll carried out by state television and broadcast on Sunday.
The Social Democrats are pinning their hopes on forming a coalition with the rightist People's Party, which clinched one of their highest poll scores to date in Delo with 7.5 percent.
The two parties have formed a loose pre-electoral pact with the conservative Christian Democrats, headed by former prime minister Lojze Peterle.
Peterle's party fared poorly in the three polls, with support ranging from 5.4 in Delo to 3.7 in Dnevnik, compared to the more than 16 percent of votes it won in the 1992 election.
Backing for the United List of Social Democrats, the former communist party, ranged from 5.7 percent in Delo to four percent in the television survey.
